chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Two-beat versus four-beat, and playing pretty solos
summary: He prefers four beats and swing to New Orleans two-beat, calls his music modern Dixieland, and likes playing pretty ballads.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: What about - a lot of people make a big deal about two-beat and four-beat jazz---
Well, it's a funny thing -- I never went for the two-beat jazz - rhythm section -

Four rhythm sections all my life -- I've heard those by bands and I never could play much with those two - four guys - you know - two beats on the base drum, two..buh-buh on the base -you know - I like the four beats---
Right. Is that strictly New Orleans stuff?

Oh, sure. You know, it's a George Lewis type of music; I've never been very good at that kind of thing--- I always considered what I played modern Dixie-land and Swing--- and I think Swing is what I like better.
And, if they choose to call it Chicago style jazz - why that's their business---
That is their business-- yes. Let them call me what they like---
But, the point is you know too that I have made --- I've always liked to play pretty solos--- which is a completely - again - away from any style at all---
Yeah - so-called any style--- just some pretty solos--- I think all the jazz musicians like to do that--- play little medleys of songs that are pretty and it's a nice contrast from the Dixie-land--
And, you do the same - but it's still the jazz because you're doing your improvising on those so-called pretty ballads--
